issues.description: concatenatedRSToASN1DER encodes r and s into two throwaway ASN1Encoder instances before re-encoding them in the return statement.
issues.knownIssueText: Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.

earlierComments.text: Dead computation: the two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls allocate encoders and encode rBigInteger/sBigInteger, but their results are discarded — the returned DER comes entirely from the expression at lines 117-121, which re-encodes the same BigIntegers. These two statements have no effect and should be removed (they are a leftover from an earlier formulation).

Remove these two discarded encoder writes. Each allocates an encoder and encodes a BigInteger, but neither result participates in the returned signature; lines 119–120 repeat both writes on fresh encoders. This performs redundant encoding and allocations on every concatenated-signature conversion.

The two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` encode values and discard the results. The return expression re-encodes the same values, so these lines are dead computation left over from a copy-paste or refactor. Remove them.

issues.description: order() is added to CryptoProvider as an abstract method, breaking source and binary compatibility for existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations.
issues.knownIssueText: Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

earlierComments.text: order() was added as an abstract method to the public CryptoProvider interface. CryptoIntegration.detectProvider now invokes order() on every ServiceLoader-discovered CryptoProvider via Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order). Any CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface (an external or separately built provider jar on the classpath) will throw AbstractMethodError at detection time, i.e. during AuthzClient.create()/server bootstrap, before any provider is usable. Giving order() a default implementation (e.g. default int order() { return 0; }) avoids the binary-incompatibility.

issues.description: detectProvider no longer fails when several crypto providers are present; with Default, FIPS and Elytron all at order 200, ties are resolved by classpath order and a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS provider.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: detectProvider sorts by order() reversed and silently picks index 0, removing the previous multiple-providers error. WHY: Default/FIPS/Elytron all return order 200, so ambiguous classpath (e.g. default+FIPS) now nondeterministically picks one by ServiceLoader order instead of failing fast, risking wrong FIPS vs non-FIPS crypto. HOW: only auto-ignore lower-order providers; throw when the top two have equal order().

Reject ambiguous highest-priority providers rather than silently taking the first. Both DefaultCryptoProvider and FIPS1402Provider return order 200 in this PR, so when both are present the stable sort leaves the decision to ServiceLoader discovery order. A deployment expecting FIPS can therefore initialize the ordinary Bouncy Castle provider without an error; previously this mixed classpath failed closed. Preserve the error for tied highest-priority providers (or require an explicit security-mode/provider choice), while still allowing the lower-priority authz-client fallback.

detectProvider() no longer fails fast when multiple CryptoProviders are present and instead silently picks the first after sorting by order() descending. All Keycloak providers return the same order (DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider all return 200), so a tie between two providers is broken by the non-deterministic ServiceLoader iteration order rather than the intended priority. The previous code threw an IllegalStateException forcing the classpath to be corrected; now a deployment with two provider jars (exactly the 'multiple providers on classpath' scenario this PR enables) can silently select the unintended provider — e.g. a non-FIPS/strict provider when FIPS is required — with no error. Use a stable tie-breaker (delegate to the provider name/type) or reject equal top orders instead of relying on ServiceLoader order.

issues.description: Claims a wrong-length JOSE signature causes an unchecked exception in concatenatedRSToASN1DER; verifiers catch it and report verification failure, as with the existing providers.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER splits signature without validating signature.length==signLength. WHY: short JOSE input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException and long input is silently truncated to signLength, breaking the ECDSACryptoProvider contract (IOException on malformed) used by verifier contexts. HOW: check length upfront and throw IOException.

concatenatedRSToASN1DER never validates signature.length == signLength before System.arraycopy(signature,0,r,1,len) / (signature,len,s,1,len). A short JWS signature throws unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of the declared IOException, breaking verification on attacker-controlled input. Validate length and throw IOException.

issues.description: The ES384 and ES512 tests sign with the same default P-256 key, so the converter is never tested with real P-384 or P-521 signatures.

earlierComments.text: Single default EC keypair reused for ES256/ES384/ES512: testES384/testES512 names claim larger curves but body signs with the same P-256 key and only pads to larger signLength, so full-width 384/521-bit handling is never exercised. Generate a per-algorithm keypair with the correct curve (e.g. secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) before signing.

Every case generates a default EC key rather than a key on the curve associated with the named algorithm. On the standard JDK this is P-256, so testES384 and testES512 just pad P-256 signature components to larger lengths. A converter that discards nonzero high bytes beyond 32 bytes would still pass all three cases. Initialize the key generator with the appropriate curve per case (P-256, P-384, and P-521) so the larger-component conversions are actually tested.

Generate a key on the curve corresponding to each tested algorithm rather than using the provider's default EC curve for all three tests. On the standard JDK this generates a P-256 key even for testES384 and testES512, so those tests merely pad P-256 integers to larger output lengths and never exercise actual P-384/P-521 signature encoding (including P-521's long-form sequence length).

issues.description: The test only checks a round trip between the two new converters and never verifies the re-encoded DER against the original signature or with Signature.verify, so mutually consistent bugs go undetected.

earlierComments.text: Tautological round-trip assertion: rsConcat2 is derived from rsConcat via encode+decode that are inverses if self-consistent, so assertArrayEquals(rsConcat,rsConcat2) passes even if both directions are wrong. Verify against external oracle: Signature.initVerify + verify(asn1Des) and/or compare rsConcat to expected split, not just to itself.

The test only checks self-consistency: it asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(g(asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign))) == asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign), i.e. that concatenatedRSToASN1DER is a right inverse of asn1derToConcatenatedRS. It never compares against the original DER `sign`, never verifies the ECDSA signature, and never asserts the emvider output is canonical DER. Because the decoder it reads back with (ASN1Decoder.readLength) accepts non-canonical long-form lengths (e.g. 0x81) and validates only tag numbers, a regression in ASN1Encoder.writeLength that always emitted long form would still round-trip and the test would still pass, even though the produced signature would no longer be valid DER and would be rejected by the Keycloak server / a JDK Signature.verify. Assert the encoded signature is valid DER (e.g. verify it with a JDK Signature, or compare asn1derToConcatenatedRS(sign) against a known-good width-padded r||s and assert its length equals algorithm.getSignatureLength()).

The assertion only establishes agreement between the two new conversion routines, not correctness of the converted signature. For example, swapping r and s in both routines makes this entire round trip pass, although the DER result no longer verifies the signed data. Verify `asn1Des` with the public key and original data (or compare against an independently specified encoding) so mutually compensating conversion defects fail the test.

issues.description: getBouncyCastleProvider in AuthzClientCryptoProvider returns the JDK default KeyStore provider instead of BouncyCastle, contrary to the CryptoProvider contract.
ASN1Decoder.readInteger accepts constructed INTEGER tags because it only masks the low tag bits, so malformed DER is parsed as valid.
The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.knownIssueText: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

earlierComments.text: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.description: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

earlierComments.text: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.description: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

earlierComments.text: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.description: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

earlierComments.text: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.description: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

earlierComments.text: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.description: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

earlierComments.text: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.description: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.
remove() always queries idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias), adding a database lookup on every IDP removal even when the cached entry already holds the model.

registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early when the IDP stays a login IDP with the same organizationId without comparing BROKER_PUBLIC, so toggling kc.org.broker.public on a realm-level IDP leaves the login caches stale.

earlierComments.text: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate returns early whenever the IDP stays a login IDP and its organizationId is unchanged, without comparing the BROKER_PUBLIC config value. For a realm-level IDP (organizationId == null) the new predicate at IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 short-circuits to true, so toggling kc.org.broker.public changes neither the predicate nor the org id, yet the ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches (which, per the default getForLogin, include realm-level IDPs whose BROKER_PUBLIC=true) are left stale — the login page then keeps showing an IDP whose BROKER_PUBLIC was cleared, or omits one that was just made public. Also invalidate when the BROKER_PUBLIC value differs between original and updated (or when the IDP's org-public status changes).

issues.description: The constant IDP_LOGIN_SUFFIX is used as an infix in cacheKeyForLogin (realmId.idp.login.MODE), unlike its sibling *_SUFFIX constants, so the name misstates the key format.

earlierComments.text: The constant is named IDP_LOGIN_SUFFIX, matching its siblings IDP_COUNT_KEY_SUFFIX / IDP_ALIAS_KEY_SUFFIX / IDP_ORG_ID_KEY_SUFFIX which all terminate the cache key, but cacheKeyForLogin (line 78) uses it as an infix: `realm.getId() + IDP_LOGIN_SUFFIX + "." + fetchMode` produces "realmId.idp.login.REALM_ONLY", not a key ending in ".idp.login". The name states a position the code does not use; a maintainer reading the name (or copying the sibling pattern) will misjudge the key format. Rename it (e.g. IDP_LOGIN_KEY_INFIX / IDP_LOGIN_SEGMENT) or move it to the end of the key so name and usage agree.

issues.description: The cache-hit path of getForLogin collects IDPs into a HashSet and streams it, so results come in hash order instead of the delegate's order returned on a miss, making ordering differ by cache state.

earlierComments.text: The cached path resolves the IDPs into a fresh `HashSet` and returns `identityProviders.stream()`, so the returned order is HashSet iteration order (derived from element hashCodes), not the order the delegate produces. On a cache miss (line 218) and in the null-id fallback (line 249) the delegate's stream/order is returned directly. Consumers therefore see the same IDPs in a different, nondeterministic order depending on whether the cache was hit, which can change UI listing order. Preserve the cached IDs' order (e.g. use a LinkedHashSet / LinkedHashMap keyed by the cached internal IDs) so cache-hit and cache-miss return a consistent ordering.

issues.description: The OrganizationCacheTest create/remove step only adds and removes non-login IDPs, so it would pass even if registerIDPLoginInvalidation were deleted from create() and remove().

earlierComments.text: The test only exercises the negative create/remove case: the IDP added (`idp-alias-20`, `hideOnLogin(true)`) and the IDP removed (`idp-alias-1`, disabled) are both non-login IDPs, so only the `getLoginPredicate() == false` branch of `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` is hit. Since step 1 only asserts the login caches are still present (`assertNotNull`), and steps 2-4 only touch the update path, the entire test passes even if `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(model)` in `create()` and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)` in `remove()` are deleted. The test therefore does not verify that creating or removing a login-capable IDP invalidates the login caches — a new behaviour introduced by this PR. Add a case that, after the caches are populated, creates (and/or removes) an enabled, non-hidden IDP and asserts the login caches are cleared.

issues.description: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.knownIssueText: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

earlierComments.text: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.description: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.knownIssueText: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.description: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.knownIssueText: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.description: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.knownIssueText: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

earlierComments.text: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.description: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

earlierComments.text: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.description: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

earlierComments.text: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.description: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

earlierComments.text: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.description: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

earlierComments.text: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.description: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.
AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName handles only USERS, so for the new CLIENTS resource type the admin API returns a null/UUID display name instead of 'All clients' or the clientId.

earlierComments.text: The Clients resource type was added to `getOrCreateResource` but not to the sibling `getResourceName` (same file, ~line 310), which only handles USERS. For a Clients permission, PolicyResourceService.java:218 gets a null display name for per-client resources, whose name is the client's internal id. The "all clients" resource also gets no "All clients" label. Add a `CLIENTS` branch to `getResourceName`: return "All clients" for the type resource, otherwise look up the client by id and return its clientId.

The new CLIENTS resource type was wired into getOrCreateResource but not into the sibling per-resource-type switch in getResourceName (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:304-326), which still only special-cases USERS ("All users" / username). For a CLIENTS policy the method now falls through to resource.getDisplayName(); per-client resources are created with only a UUID name (line 104) and the type resource is named "Clients", so PolicyResourceService.getResources() (PolicyResourceService.java:218) returns a null/UUID displayName for client FGAP resources where users get a friendly name. Add the parallel branch: "All clients" for the type resource and the client's clientId otherwise.

issues.description: When the server rejects an email, the signup form marks it with the generic 'invalid email' text instead of the server's reason (blocked or not allowed).

earlierComments.text: The message shown for a rejected email disagrees with the reason the code is reacting to. This branch fires when the server rejected the email (result.errors.email), and this PR gives that condition its own server string — user.email.blocked, added in config/locales/server.en.yml as "is not allowed." — but the client re-labels it with the generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid'). A user whose address is perfectly well-formed but blocked/hosted on a blacklisted domain is therefore told their email is invalid, contradicting the reason just returned by the server. Use the blocked/not-allowed message (and add a matching client locale key) instead of user.email.invalid. Notice the same generic string is used at line ~94 for validation failures, so it should not be reused to represent a distinct server-side rejection.

issues.description: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email with a case-sensitive exact match and no normalisation, so changing the letter case of a blocked address bypasses the block list.
issues.knownIssueText: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

earlierComments.text: Blocked-email lookup compares the raw email without normalizing its domain. A signup for block@SPAMFROMHOME.ORG does not match a blocked record for block@spamfromhome.org despite identifying the same mailbox, allowing the signup restriction to be bypassed by changing domain capitalization. Normalize domains using Email.downcase both when storing blocked emails and when looking them up.

Canonicalize blocked emails consistently with the application's Email.downcase identity handling, both when storing entries and when looking them up. This exact equality query is case-sensitive, and BlockedEmail's validation callback only defaults action_type. A block-list entry such as `Block@SpamFromHome.org` therefore does not block the same identity submitted/stored as `block@spamfromhome.org`. This is particularly relevant to the explicitly supported manually populated block list. Normalize existing/imported entries as well as new ones, and add a test with differing casing between the stored entry and the lookup.
Case-sensitivity bypass: BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is exact case-sensitive with no normalization, while sibling checks are case-insensitive. Normalize (downcase/strip) on write and lookup.

issues.description: BlockedEmail.should_block? updates match_count and last_match_at as a side effect of email validation, so each signup attempt (validated twice) inflates the counter and concurrent updates can lose increments.
issues.knownIssueText: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: should_block? mutates match_count/last_match_at via read-modify-write save inside a validator. WHY: Every validation call (including re-validations of the same attempt or attempts failing on unrelated fields like username) inflates stats, and concurrent signups lose increments with no atomic update. HOW: Move stats update out of validation or use atomic increment (update_counters/increment_counter) only on actual blocked rejections.

WHAT: `should_block?` mutates state (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, calls `record.save`) inside a method that is invoked from the model validation callback, and the signup controller runs validation twice per attempt (`user.valid?` at users_controller.rb:168 then `user.save` at :172). WHY: a single signup attempt increments `match_count` twice and rewrites `last_match_at`, so the per-email block statistics the feature was built to track are wrong. HOW: make the read side non-mutating for validation and record the match separately (e.g. move the increment out of validation, or guard it so it runs once per attempt), keeping the predicate pure.

WHAT: `record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save` is a non-atomic read-modify-write with no lock or unique constraint protection. WHY: two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same `match_count` and one write overwrites the other, losing counts, so the tracked statistics drift under load. HOW: use an atomic update such as `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all('match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...')` or a database-level counter increment.

issues.description: Claims the 'returns false' spec cannot distinguish nil from false because be_false is a truthiness matcher.

earlierComments.text: This test is named "returns false if a record with the email doesn't exist," but it cannot verify that. `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns `record && record.action_type == actions[:block]`, which yields `nil` (not `false`) when no record exists, and under this suite's RSpec 2 semantics `subject.should be_false` is a truthiness matcher that passes for any falsy value including `nil`. The assertion therefore passes on the nil the code actually returns and would only fail on an outright `true`; it does not pin the `false`/`nil` distinction its name asserts. Assert the value exactly (e.g. `subject.should == false`, or `be_falsey`/`be_nil` if nil is intended) so a regression returning a non-false falsy value is caught.

issues.description: The domain whitelist/blacklist regex @(domains) is not anchored at the end, so an address like user@example.com.evil.com matches a whitelist entry for example.com and bypasses the restriction.
issues.knownIssueText: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: email_in_restriction_setting? builds unanchored Regexp "@(domains)" with only '.' escaped. WHY: Whitelist 'gmail.com' substring-matches 'victim@gmail.com.evil.com', so an attacker registers with an unapproved domain and bypasses the allow-list; blacklist similarly over/under-matches and other regex metachars are unescaped. HOW: Anchor and escape domains (e.g. Regexp.escape per domain split on '|' plus /\A[^@\s]+@(?:domain)\z/i).

issues.description: Emails rejected by the server are cached in rejectedEmails for the controller's lifetime and never cleared, so an address that later becomes valid keeps failing client-side validation until reload.
A spec comment says last_match_at shows whether an email has ever been blocked, but should_block? updates it on every match, including do_nothing records.
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as well as MANAGE, so an admin with only view permission on all groups passes manage checks such as group creation.
issues.knownIssueText: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

earlierComments.text: The no-arg canManage() returns true when the caller holds only an all-groups VIEW permission (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`), whereas the per-group canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) requires MANAGE. WHAT: a caller with only the view scope on all groups is treated as having manage rights. WHY: canManage()/requireManage() gate group creation and other manage operations (e.g. GroupsResource.addGroup -> auth.groups().requireManage()), so a read-only viewer of all groups can create/manage groups — privilege escalation. HOW: drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() only returns true for MANAGE, aligning it with canManage(GroupModel): `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`

GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 70) evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE), identical to canView() at line 52, so a caller granted only the VIEW scope on the all-groups resource is treated as a group manager. The per-group overload canManage(GroupModel) (line 79) correctly requires only MANAGE, and AdminPermissionsSchema defines MANAGE as the manage scope for GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, so the two checks disagree. requireManage() therefore succeeds for read-only administrators, letting them create/update/delete groups, add subgroups and map group roles. Drop VIEW from the scope list so canManage() checks MANAGE only.

WHAT: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage on VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). WHY: A caller with only view-all-groups permission passes the manage check, allowing group creation/management reserved for manage. HOW: Check only MANAGE, e.g. hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE).

issues.description: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses the authorization resource id instead of the resource name (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, so per-group view-members grants are not resolved and user filtering gets wrong ids.
issues.knownIssueText: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses authz resource IDs (groupResource.getId()) as group IDs and looks them up via findByName. WHY: Resource names equal group IDs (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId()), so findByName(resourceId) misses and the returned set contains unusable IDs, breaking user search/count filtering by group. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() like V1 does (resource.getName().substring prefix / name) for both the hasPermission lookup and the granted set.

findByType callback passes groupResource.getId() to hasPermission() and granted set, but AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup defines resource name (not UUID) as groupId and hasPermission looks up via findByName(server, groupId). Use groupResource.getName() for both check and granted set, otherwise lookups miss to all-groups fallback and callers receive authz UUIDs instead of group IDs.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses groupResource.getId() for lookup and result collection, but V2 group resources are named with the group ID (resolveGroup returns group.getId()) and hasPermission does findByName. Use groupResource.getName() in both places to evaluate the correct per-group resource and to return actual group IDs.

issues.description: Per-group resources are created without the Groups type, so getGroupIdsWithViewPermission's findByType never sees specific group grants.

earlierComments.text: findByType(GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE) does not enumerate the specific group resources created by AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, because that method creates them without setting their type. Consequently, specific VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are omitted from the group IDs used for user counts and database filtering. Assign the Groups type to specific group resources and ensure the all-Groups resource is not treated as a model group.

issues.description: The user search filter still requires legacy 'group.resource.<id>' resources, so with V2 group permissions the members of authorized groups are excluded from user searches.

earlierComments.text: The new V2 group permission IDs are passed into a JPA filter that still requires a legacy group.resource.<groupId> authorization resource. JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery checks for that prefixed name, whereas AdminPermissionsSchema creates V2 group resources named only with the group ID, so authorized group members are excluded from user searches even with valid group IDs. Update the database filtering path to support V2 resource naming rather than requiring a legacy V1 resource.

issues.description: The new Javadoc for requireManageMembers points to canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers.

earlierComments.text: The javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false, but this method is the require-variant of canManageMembers, not canManageMembership. The text was copied from requireManageMembership above it. It should reference canManageMembers so the documented contract matches the method name and behavior.

The Javadoc for requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. It should refer to canManageMembers(GroupModel), which is a different check, so the doc misdescribes the method.

Javadoc for requireManageMembers references canManageMembership instead of canManageMembers (copy-paste). Fix link to {@link #canManageMembers(GroupModel)} so the contract describes the method it guards.

issues.description: The Javadoc of getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says it returns a Stream though the method returns a Set.

earlierComments.text: The Javadoc for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission says it returns a 'Stream of IDs', but the method returns Set<String>. Change the @return text to describe a Set of group IDs.
@return says 'Stream of IDs' but method returns Set<String> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. Fix doc to 'Set of IDs' to match the signature.

The new @return documentation promises a Stream of IDs, but the method declares Set<String> and both implementations return sets. Describe a set of IDs instead, so the documented return contract matches what callers actually receive.

issues.description: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission runs a full permission evaluation for every group resource on each user search and count, costing O(groups) policy evaluations per request.

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission passes getResourceTypeResource's result to policyStore.findByResource without a null check, causing an NPE and 500 on group listing and user search when the Groups type resource is missing.

Removing the canViewGlobal short-circuit from the subgroup and group listings makes an admin with an all-groups V2 grant run one full authorization evaluation per group in the listing instead of a single check.
GroupPermissionEvaluator.canView() Javadoc promises VIEW/MANAGE permission grants access, but the V1 GroupPermissions implementation only checks admin roles.
isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, so only team owners pass; team admins who are not organizer or attendee are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN.
issues.knownIssueText: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.

The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

issues.description: The guest blacklist is lowercased but incoming guest emails are compared without normalization, so a blacklisted address submitted with different casing bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS and is added and emailed.
issues.knownIssueText: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).

WHAT: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS entries are lowercased but the incoming guest string is compared without lowercasing/normalizing. WHY: an attacker bypasses the blocklist with case variation (e.g. Spam@Example.com) and gets added/emailed.

issues.description: The server never deduplicates the guests array, so a request with the same email twice inserts duplicate attendee rows for the booking.
issues.knownIssueText: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: uniqueGuests filter only dedupes against existing booking.attendees with case-sensitive === and never dedupes duplicates within the input guests array itself (server schema has no uniqueness refine unlike the client). WHY: a request with the same new email twice creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany.

uniqueGuests filters only against existing attendees/blacklist but never dedupes guests[] itself and schema has no uniqueness check. A request like guests=[a@x.com,a@x.com] passes the filter twice and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows or throws an unhandled DB unique-constraint exception. Dedupe/normalize input (and reject intra-request duplicates) before createMany.

uniqueGuests filters against existing attendees but does not deduplicate addresses within the incoming guests array. A direct mutation with the same new address twice inserts two Attendee records and sends duplicate invitations because the server schema permits duplicates and the Attendee model has no unique booking/email constraint. Deduplicate normalized input before filtering and inserting.

issues.description: Check-then-insert without a transaction or unique constraint lets two concurrent addGuests calls for the same email both pass the existing-attendee check and create duplicate attendees.

earlierComments.text: Race condition: findFirst check for existing attendees then booking.update+createMany is not atomic. Two concurrent addGuests calls with the same new email both see it as absent and both insert, creating duplicates. Guard with a unique constraint and handle conflict or run in a transaction/serializable check.

Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

issues.description: Attendee authorization and existing-attendee dedup compare emails case-sensitively, so an attendee with differently-cased stored email is FORBIDDEN and a case-variant of an existing attendee is added again.

earlierComments.text: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

issues.description: The handler passes the unfiltered guests list to sendAddGuestsEmails, which uses it to pick who gets AttendeeScheduledEmail, so existing attendees included in the request receive a new-booking confirmation instead of the add-guests email.
issues.knownIssueText: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: already-existing attendees included in the request are misclassified as newGuests in email-manager and receive AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (wrong notification).

Dead-transform / wrong input: `uniqueGuests` is computed (dedup vs existing attendees + blacklist) and written to DB, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the original `guests`. Existing attendees re-submitted are then `includes()`-matched as new and get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

Pass `uniqueGuests` (the filtered set written to DB) to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of raw `guests`; the email layer assumes newGuests exactly equals newly created attendees for its Scheduled vs AddGuests branch.

issues.description: EventManager is created with the requesting user's credentials, so when a non-organizer adds guests the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the wrong account is used) for references without a credentialId.

earlierComments.text: EventManager is initialized with the requesting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's credentials. When an attendee or team owner adds guests to a booking whose calendar reference lacks credentialId, updateAllCalendarEvents selects credentials by type from the caller's calendars, so the organizer's event is not updated or the update targets the wrong account. Load credentials for booking.userId and initialize the manager with the booking owner.

issues.description: Claims a failing calendar update at addGuests.handler.ts:165 aborts the mutation after guests are persisted; the calendar update path already swallows provider errors.

earlierComments.text: The attendees are written to the database at line 92, but `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 runs outside the try/catch. If it throws, the mutation returns an error even though the guests are already persisted, so the DB and the calendar are out of sync. No emails are sent, and a retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid'. Catch and handle the calendar update failure after the DB write.

The attendees are already committed to the DB when `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited without a try/catch. If the calendar sync throws, the mutation returns an error and skips the emails, although the guests were added. The caller sees a failure for a partly applied change and may retry. Handle calendar sync failure as best-effort, as the email send is, or run it before the DB write.

issues.description: Claims any attendee can add guests and trigger invites; this is the deliberate permission model of the new feature.

earlierComments.text: Any attendee, matched only by email, is allowed to add arbitrary guests to a booking, and the handler then sends emails and calendar invites on the organizer's behalf. Any attendee can use this to send invites to arbitrary addresses. Restrict the action to the organizer and team admins, or verify that the attendee's email is confirmed.

issues.description: The guests array has no server-side size limit, so any authorized caller, including an attendee, can add thousands of guests and trigger an unbounded batch of inserts and emails.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: guests is an unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: any authorized caller (including a mere attendee) can submit thousands of emails causing unbounded createMany inserts plus unbounded Promise.all email fanout in sendAddGuestsEmails.

The mutation accepts an unbounded guest array that is persisted and immediately expanded into concurrent emails to every attendee. For non-seated bookings each email's ICS serializes the full attendee list, so adding N guests creates O(N) concurrent sends and O(N²) aggregate attachment work; repeated additions also resend to all existing attendees. Enforce a server-side guest-count and total-attendee limit before insertion and bound notification concurrency.

issues.description: The Remove email tooltip in MultiEmail is a hard-coded English string instead of a translation key.

earlierComments.text: Tooltip content="Remove email" is hard-coded English user-facing text bypassing i18n while surrounding strings in the same file/PR use t(). Wrap it in t() e.g. content={t("remove_email")} and add the key to locales.

`Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

The new removal tooltip hard-codes `Remove email`, so users in non-English locales see English text even though the neighbouring controls use `t(...)` and this component already obtains `t` from useLocale. Route this tooltip through a translation key (and supply its English translation) rather than using the literal.

issues.description: The onError fallback to unable_to_add_guests is unreachable because the template-string message is always truthy.

earlierComments.text: Unreachable fallback: `message` is a template string `${code}: ${...}` which is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` never takes the fallback. Build message conditionally or test the underlying parts for emptiness.

In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

The error message is built as a template string, so it is always truthy. The `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback is therefore dead code, and the user can see "undefined: ..." or an untranslated raw message. Use `err.message ? t(err.message) : t("unable_to_add_guests")`.

issues.description: After a validation failure followed by a successful add, isInvalidEmail stays true, so the stale emails_must_be_unique_valid error shows the next time the dialog is opened.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one failed validation the red emails_must_be_unique_valid error persists on the next open/successful add.

issues.description: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, so hosts and attendees receive add-guests emails even when standard emails are disabled.
issues.knownIssueText: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

issues.description: The add-guests handler omits booking.iCalUID from the CalendarEvent, so the add-guests emails' .ics attachments use booking.uid as UID and recipients' calendars treat them as a new event rather than an update of the original booking invite.
The addGuests FORBIDDEN error uses the translation key you_do_not_have_permission, which is missing from the locale files, so the dialog shows the raw key to users.
The comment in MultiEmailLazy.tsx ("These are like 40kb") is copied from the phone input lazy loader and does not apply to MultiEmail, which only uses existing UI components.
addGuests does not check the booking status, so guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, which updates calendars and emails invitations for events that no longer exist.
Guest email uniqueness is checked case-sensitively, so case variants of the same address are accepted as distinct guests (and slip past the lowercased blacklist).
Adding guests ignores `seatsPerTimeSlot`, so a seated event can exceed its configured capacity; reject when attendees plus new guests exceed the seat limit.
The PR creates a shared MultiEmail component in packages/ui but leaves the inline multiemail copy in form-builder Components.tsx, so two copies of the same widget exist.

earlierComments.text: The PR extracts this helper into `packages/ui` (and registers it in `packages/ui/index.tsx:153`), but the pre-existing copy of the exact same helper was left behind in `packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx:231-313` (its own `multiemail` factory, still carrying the now-stale comment "TODO: Make it a ui component"). The sibling was not updated to consume the new shared component, so the codebase now has two divergent copies of the same guest/email list widget — the duplicate will silently drift from the shared one. Point the form-builder factory at `@calcom/ui`'s `MultiEmail` (or remove the inline copy).

issues.description: The Lithuanian TOTP setup step was replaced with Italian text in both the account and login bundles.
issues.knownIssueText: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).

earlierComments.text: The Lithuanian OTP setup instruction has been replaced with an Italian sentence. login-config-totp.ftl renders this message directly, so users selecting Lithuanian receive an instruction in the wrong language; the same copied sentence also appears in the Lithuanian account bundle at line 101. Replace both values with the Lithuanian translation of the new installation instruction.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian (“Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare”), but this is the Lithuanian locale and the surrounding setup steps are Lithuanian. Translate the new instruction into Lithuanian rather than copying the Italian translation. The same incorrect replacement appears in the login bundle at themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties:71 and should be corrected there too; otherwise Lithuanian users see an untranslated first step in both OTP setup flows.

The replacement OTP setup instruction is Italian, not Lithuanian (`Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare`). The same replacement was made for `totpStep1` in the Lithuanian account bundle. Translate both replacements into Lithuanian so selecting Lithuanian does not display Italian instructions during authenticator setup.

issues.description: The zh_CN totpStep1 translation is written in Traditional Chinese instead of Simplified Chinese.
issues.knownIssueText: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.

earlierComments.text: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) file was given Traditional Chinese characters: totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：. Compare the unchanged neighbouring lines (e.g. '打开应用扫描二维码…') which use Simplified forms; 手機/應用程式/安裝 are Traditional. zh_CN must be Simplified Chinese, so this string is in the wrong script/variant for the locale.
totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN uses Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式), not Simplified Chinese as the rest of the file does. Replace it with the Simplified form: 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：
The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). Use the Simplified form, "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

issues.description: The method santizeAnchors is misspelled; it should be sanitizeAnchors.
issues.knownIssueText: The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').

issues.description: HTML_TAGS is a non-static, non-private field instead of a private static final constant.
issues.knownIssueText: Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

issues.description: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

earlierComments.text: The common prefix (start) and common suffix (end) are computed independently and can overlap, for example value "aa" vs sanitized "a". Then substring(start, length - end) gets begin > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so that start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()), e.g. `while (end < min - start && ...)`.

The common prefix and common suffix are computed independently and can overlap, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` can have start > end and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This crashes the verifier instead of reporting 'Illegal HTML'. Cap the suffix scan with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

WHAT: Common prefix/suffix stripping for the diff message can compute start+end larger than the string length and call substring(start, length-end) with start > end. WHY: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the key loop and crashes verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. HOW: Clamp end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. stop suffix scan when end >= length-start.

issues.description: normalizeValue blanks the entire choice expression for some keys before HTML validation, so markup placed inside a choice branch of those keys bypasses the new verifier.

earlierComments.text: Choice normalization removes all branch content before HTML validation, allowing prohibited markup to bypass the new translation policy. A translated error-invalid-multivalued-size value such as `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1

WHAT: normalizeValue replaces the entire {n,choice,...} block with ... before sanitizing, so HTML inside choice options is never checked. WHY: A translation can smuggle tags (e.g. {2,choice,0#<script>...}) in error-invalid-multivalued-size/linkExpirationFormatter keys and pass the verifier, reaching UI rendering as XSS. HOW: Sanitize/validate the choice body instead of blanking it, or run the HTML policy on the inner choice text as well.

issues.description: The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

earlierComments.text: The admin-ui bundle is consumed by react-i18next, which interpolates with double-brace `{{0}}` syntax (the previous value was `Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}}`). This line was rewritten to Java MessageFormat/ICU syntax (`{0}` ... `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), which i18next does not understand: the placeholders will not be substituted and the literal `{2,choice,...}` text will be shown to users. Keep the JS-side value in `{{0}}` form (and don't introduce ICU ChoiceFormat into the JS bundle); the ICU/choice spelling belongs only in the Java theme properties.

Same contract break in the account-ui bundle: the value was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` (i18next double-brace interpolation) and was changed to `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` MessageFormat+ICU syntax. The account console's i18next based consumer was not updated to match, so interpolation will fail and the raw placeholder/choice syntax will be rendered. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders for the JS bundle.

The account-ui bundle is consumed by i18next, which interpolates with double braces (the original string was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`). This PR aligned the value to the Java theme convention, replacing `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` with `{0}/{1}/{2}` and adding ICU `{2,choice,...}`. i18next will no longer substitute the placeholders and cannot interpret the ICU choice, so the account UI shows the raw `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and literal choice text. Keep the JS-side double-brace form for this bundle (adapt the choice accordingly) rather than the Java single-brace/ICU form used by the theme messages.

issues.description: If the English counterpart of a messages_*.properties file does not exist, verifySafeHtml throws an unchecked RuntimeException that escapes the mojo, crashing the build instead of reporting a validation message.
The theme verifier's HTML and anchor regexes are case-sensitive, so uppercase tags in translations are flagged as illegal HTML by the build.

The anchor regex </?a[^>]*> in the theme verifier treats any tag starting with 'a' (<abbr>, <area>, ...) as an anchor tag, which can produce misleading anchor errors or strip such tags before HTML sanitizing.
The anchor-mismatch error in VerifyMessageProperties omits the message key and file, so the failing translation is hard to locate, unlike the 'Illegal HTML' message.
testFeatureNotEnabled only covers the metadata subcommand, so the feature guard in the check subcommand is untested.

earlierComments.text: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches the `metadata` subcommand and never the `check` subcommand. Removing the feature guard from UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() would therefore not fail any test. It also doesn't assert the exit code (FEATURE_DISABLED=4). Add a case for `check` and assert the exit code on both.

WHAT: testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand disabled path and never the check subcommand. WHY: the feature gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run can be removed or broken without failing any test since no assertion covers its disabled message/exit code. HOW: also launch/assert the check command without --features (e.g. parameterize over metadata and check subcommands or add a second Launch).

testFeatureNotEnabled only exercises the metadata subcommand, leaving the identical ROLLING_UPDATES gate in UpdateCompatibilityCheck unverified. If the Check gate were removed, the suite still passes. Parameterize/add a second @Launch for {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME} (with required --file or not) asserting the disabled message and FEATURE_DISABLED exit code.

issues.description: The disabled-feature test checks only the error message, not that the command exits with FEATURE_DISABLED (4).

earlierComments.text: The new disabled-feature test only verifies the error text, not the failure exit status. If the metadata command still prints this diagnostic but exits with 0 (or another incorrect code) instead of FEATURE_DISABLED (4), this test would still pass. Assert that cliResult.exitCode() equals CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED so the test actually protects the new disabled-feature failure contract.

issues.description: testMissingOptionOnSave only asserts a message is absent, so it would still pass if --features=rolling-updates were not honoured and the command failed with the feature-disabled error.
The working-hours check computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, so slots that start within working hours but end after them are accepted.
issues.knownIssueText: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

earlierComments.text: WHAT: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()` — an exact duplicate of `start` — instead of using `slotEndTime`. WHY: the working-hours upper-bound test `end > workingHour.endTime` therefore compares the slot START against the working-day end, so a slot whose start is inside working hours but whose end (start + eventLength) overruns `workingHour.endTime` is never filtered and is reported as available, allowing bookings outside the host's working hours. HOW: compute `const end = slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute();`.

`end` is computed from `slotStartTime` instead of `slotEndTime`, so it always equals `start`. The `end > workingHour.endTime` check is identical to the `start` check and never catches a slot that starts within working hours but ends past them. Use `slotEndTime.hour() * 60 + slotEndTime.minute()` for `end`.

`end` is computed identically to `start` (both from slotStartTime), so the check `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` can never reject a slot on the upper bound. A slot starting inside working hours but ending after workingHour.endTime is wrongly considered available; derive `end` from slotEndTime instead.

issues.description: The date-override check compares two dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, so zero-length (day off) overrides are never detected.
issues.knownIssueText: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

earlierComments.text: This compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with `===` (reference equality), which is always false, so a zero-length override (start equal to end, whole day blocked) never returns true here. Compare timestamps, e.g. `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`.

`dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate dayjs object references, so `===` is always false. The zero-length date-override branch is dead code and such an override is never recognised as covering the day; compare values (e.g. .isSame() or .valueOf() === .valueOf()) instead.

The equality check compares two separately created Dayjs objects with ===, which is always false, even when the override start and end represent the same instant. The intended zero-length/closed-day rejection is unreachable, and a slot beginning exactly at that instant can reach the dateOverrideExist success return. Compare timestamps or use isSame instead.

issues.description: When a date override exists for the day, checkIfIsAvailable returns true before checking busy times, so slots overlapping existing bookings are reported available.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: when `dateOverrideExist` is true the function returns `true` before running the `busy.every(...)` check at the end. WHY: on any day that has a matching date override, a slot inside the override is reported available without checking the host's existing bookings (`busy` is spread via `...schedule`/`...userSchedule`), so a fixed/loose host who already has a booking during the override window is still shown as free — enabling double-booking. HOW: do not return early here; fall through so the override branch only decides whether the slot is inside the override window, and let the existing `busy` evaluation decide availability (e.g. `if (dateOverrideExist) { /* within override, still check busy */ } else { /* fall through to busy */ }`).

The new `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` short-circuits the `busy` conflict check (and the workingHours check) for any slot that falls inside a date override window. Every caller of `checkIfIsAvailable` previously counted on it returning false for a slot that overlaps an existing booking; on days covered by a date override that guarantee is gone, so slots conflicting with the user's real bookings are now reported as available and can be double-booked. The override branch should let control fall through to the `busy.every(...)` check (returning true only for the availability-window part) instead of returning early.

A matching date override returns true before checking busy periods. Both fixed-host and loose-host callers pass calendar and booking conflicts in busy, so a host with an override is offered even when an existing booking overlaps the slot. Continue to the busy checks after validating the override instead of returning true.

issues.description: The working-hours check rejects a slot when any interval for the weekday excludes it, so split schedules (e.g. morning and afternoon) reject all slots.

earlierComments.text: The working-hours predicate rejects a slot if any interval on its weekday does not contain it. A split schedule of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 therefore loses every slot, since each valid slot lies outside the other interval. Require at least one matching interval to contain the full event instead of finding an interval that excludes it.

This search rejects a slot if it falls outside any working-hours window on that weekday. With split hours of 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a valid 10:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the afternoon window. Check for containment in at least one applicable window rather than finding any window that excludes the slot.

WHAT: Outside-working-hours test uses workingHours.find() returning true if ANY entry rejects the slot. WHY: With split schedules (two entries same weekday, e.g. morning+afternoon) a valid morning slot is outside the afternoon entry, find() matches and the slot is wrongly rejected as outside hours. HOW: Invert logic to accept if ANY entry contains the slot (e.g. !workingHours.some(entry contains slot) => outside).

issues.description: The date-override bound compares the slot start, not the slot end, with the override end, so slots extending past the override are accepted.

earlierComments.text: The override bounds reject only non-overlapping slots rather than requiring the entire event to fit inside an override. A fixed host with a 10:00–11:00 override accepts a 10:30–11:30 event generated from another host's availability, despite being unavailable for its final half hour. Accept only when at least one override contains both slotStartTime and slotEndTime; this also avoids rejecting a slot merely because another interval on the same date does not overlap it.

The upper bound checks whether slotStartTime is after the override end. A slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it is treated as available. Compare slotEndTime with the override end using isAfter, so the slot must fit entirely inside the override.

issues.description: The override timezone conversion keeps only hour and minute, so overrides that cross midnight in the invitee timezone become inverted ranges or are applied to the wrong day.

earlierComments.text: Timezone conversion takes only hour and minute, discarding day rollover and turning intervals crossing attendee midnight into reversed ranges. A UTC organizer's 22:00–23:00 override viewed in UTC+01:30 becomes startTime 1410 and endTime 30, which buildSlots skips because start is greater than end, removing valid availability. Preserve the converted dates and split the interval across attendee-day boundaries before building slots.

WHAT: activeOverrides are filtered by UTC day (line 206-207) before the invitee/organizer offset is applied (lines 212-224), and shifted hours are not re-bucketed across midnight. WHY: An override that shifts to the previous/next calendar day in the invitee timezone is dropped from the wrong day or applied to the wrong day, so slots show open when the organizer is off (and vice versa). HOW: Filter/bucket overrides in the invitee-local date after applying the offset, or emit split entries spanning two invitee days.

issues.description: The new working-hours check does not reject slots on weekdays that have no working-hours entry, so those slots are treated as available.

earlierComments.text: A weekday with no matching working-hours entry falls through to the busy checks and is treated as available when there are no conflicts. In round-robin events, slots generated for a loose host can consequently include a fixed host whose schedule excludes that day. Reject slots unless a working-hours interval on the slot's weekday contains the event, when no date override applies.

issues.description: checkIfIsAvailable's date-override check never rejects a slot that starts before the override start (only one that ends before it), so slots partly outside the override hours are treated as available.

The override day is computed with local-time dayjs(date.start) while the slot day is formatted in UTC, so on a server not running in UTC overrides near midnight are applied to the wrong day or skipped.
