With several date-override ranges on the same day, a slot is rejected as soon as it falls outside any one of them, so slots inside the other ranges become unavailable.

Loki split/shard queries are now interpolated with applyTemplateVariables before splitting and again on execution, so ad hoc filters are applied twice and already-substituted values are re-interpolated.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 52), but it then delegates each sub-request to runSplitQuery (line 163), which this PR also changed to call datasource.applyTemplateVariables again (querySplitting.ts:299), so each target is interpolated (and ad hoc filters applied) twice. WHY: double interpolation re-runs addAdHocFilters on an already-filtered expression; the stream-selector path masks the duplicate via labelExists() dedup in addFilterToStreamSelector (modifyQuery.ts:494), but parsed/structured-metadata labels use addFilterAsLabelFilter which does not dedup, producing duplicated label filters, and any interpolated value containing '$' can be re-interpolated. This is confirmed by the updated test expecting applyTemplateVariables toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) for a single target (1 call here + 4 sub-requests through runSplitQuery) instead of 1. HOW: interpolate only once — either remove the interpolation added to runShardSplitQuery and let runSplitQuery do it, or have splitQueriesByStreamShard pass the already-interpolated targets without re-interpolating in runSplitQuery.

The newly interpolated targets are interpolated again by DataSourceWithBackend.query when runQuery executes each split request. TemplateSrv.replace scans the resulting string again, so a variable whose literal value contains another defined variable token (for example, a log-search value containing `$other`) is expanded a second time and produces a different query from the non-splitting path; shard splitting also passes through this additional interpolation. Preserve the early interpolation needed for partitioning while ensuring already-interpolated targets are not interpolated again on execution, and test through the real backend query preparation rather than mocking runQuery.

Targets are interpolated here with `applyTemplateVariables`, including ad hoc filters, and then sent to `datasource.runQuery`, which interpolates them again through the backend path (datasource.ts:324/377). The ad hoc filters may be injected twice, and already-substituted values are re-interpolated, which can produce wrong or invalid LogQL. Interpolate only once. Either clear `scopedVars` and `filters` on the sub-requests after the first pass, or skip interpolation in `runQuery` for already-interpolated requests. The same issue applies to shardQuerySplitting.ts:52.

issues.description: runShardSplitQuery now filters empty/hidden targets before interpolation, so an expr that interpolates to an empty string is no longer dropped.

earlierComments.text: The order of operations was inverted relative to the previous contract: interpolation used to run before the `expr`/`hide` filters (interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets).filter(...)), and now the filters run on the *raw* targets before `applyTemplateVariables` is applied. Filtering on the un-interpolated `query.expr` means the previous fallback that dropped a target once variable substitution had emptied its expression no longer exists: a target like `{ expr: '$myVar' }` whose variable resolves to '' is truthy at filter time, survives, is then interpolated to `''`, and is passed into the shard splitting/execution loop as a blank query. To preserve the old contract the filters should run on the interpolated result (or the interpolated expr should be re-checked for emptiness).

issues.description: The variable in TablesList is still named duckDB although it no longer holds a DuckDB instance.

earlierComments.text: After replacing `duck.NewInMemoryDB()` with local `NewInMemoryDB()` and removing the duck import, the local `duckDB` still carries the old implementation name though it is no longer a duck DB. Rename to `db`/`sqlDB` (as done in sql_command.go) so identifier matches code.

issues.description: enableSqlExpressions returns false on both branches, so ReadQuery rejects every SQL expression query as not implemented even when the sqlExpressions feature flag is enabled.
The variable `enabled` in enableSqlExpressions holds the negated flag value, so it is true when SQL expressions are disabled and the name states the opposite of its value.
NewInMemoryDB returns a stateless stub whose methods all return 'not implemented', so its name misleads callers expecting a working in-memory database.
The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.knownIssueText: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

earlierComments.text: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.description: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.description: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

earlierComments.text: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.description: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.knownIssueText: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.description: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.description: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

earlierComments.text: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.description: The anonymous device limit is enforced only through TagDevice, which returns nil when the client-controlled device ID header is missing, so requests without the header authenticate anonymously regardless of the configured limit.

The doc comment on updateDevice says it updates a device "updated between the given times", but the function takes no times, computes the 30-day window itself and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when no row matches.
updateDevice prepends the query to the captured args inside the retried DB callback, so a SQLite lock retry runs Exec with the query duplicated in the arguments and the update fails.

Async callbacks passed to forEach after getCalendar became async are never awaited, so calendar and video cancellations run fire-and-forget, may not finish, and their errors escape the surrounding try/catch as unhandled rejections.
issues.knownIssueText: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

earlierComments.text: The async forEach callback moves calendar factory exceptions outside the surrounding try/catch because forEach discards its returned promise. An invalid encrypted Exchange credential throws during CalendarService construction, now producing an unhandled rejection while Reschedule continues and returns success instead of logging the error; the identical regression occurs in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Await Promise.all over bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...) inside the try block, or use an awaited for...of loop, so factory and deletion failures reach the catch.

The new async forEach callback is not awaited. If getCalendar rejects (for example, the dynamically imported calendar module fails to load or its service constructor throws), the callback produces a rejected promise that forEach discards; the surrounding try/catch cannot catch it. Previously a synchronous getCalendar failure reached that catch. Await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) or use an awaited for...of loop so these failures remain handled and calendar cleanup completes before rescheduling continues. Apply the same fix to the equivalent changed loop in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts.

WHAT: credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { await getCalendar; apiDeletes.push(...) }) pushes to apiDeletes asynchronously after outer code consumes it. WHY: outer apiDeletes is awaited elsewhere while async callbacks have not yet pushed, so recurring-event deletions are lost/partial and errors are unobserved. HOW: replace with for...of with await or collect promises via map + await Promise.all.

issues.description: Each import(...) in the appStore object literal runs when app-store/index.ts is imported, so all integrations still load at startup instead of lazily, while every entry becomes a promise.
The denial cache key joins name and parent folder with underscores, so different name/parent pairs can collide and a cached denial for one resource denies another until TTL expiry.
issues.knownIssueText: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

earlierComments.text: The denial cache key does not distinguish underscores inside resource and parent UIDs from its field separators. For the same namespace, user and action, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") generate the same key, so denying the first request makes Check return false for the second even if its permissions explicitly allow it. Encode the components unambiguously, for example as a JSON tuple or length-prefixed fields.

The denial cache key is not injective: for the same namespace, user and action, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. After the first request stores a denial, Check's new early cache return denies the second request without checking its permissions, even if it is allowed. Encode the components unambiguously (for example a JSON tuple or length-prefixed components) and add a test verifying that these two requests do not share a denial entry.

Make the denial-cache key encode component boundaries unambiguously (for example, length-prefix or serialize the components). For the same namespace, user and action, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` both produce the suffix `_a_b_c`. Underscores can occur in resource UIDs, so denying the first request caches a key that causes Check to immediately deny the second request without evaluating its permissions, even if that resource is allowed.

issues.description: The explicit denial-cache test seeds the cached permission as false instead of true, so it would pass without the denial-cache short-circuit and does not verify it.
issues.knownIssueText: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

earlierComments.text: This test claims to prove the permDenialCache short-circuit (service.go:116-121) denies access, but it seeds the cached permission as map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} (a deny), contradicting its comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". Because the cached set is already a deny, checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code falls through to the DB path, and the fake store also returns no permissions, so Allowed stays false. The assertion passes even if the entire permDenialCache early-return were deleted. Seed the cached permission as true (map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}) so that only the denial-cache entry can force Allowed=false; otherwise the test does not verify the feature.

The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code sets the permCache entry to `false`, which is a deny. The test therefore does not show that the permission cache is skipped. Set the value to `true`, or change the comment to match.

The 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' test would still pass if the permDenialCache check were removed. permCache is seeded with dash1:false, not true as the comment claims, so the normal path also denies. Seed permCache with {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} and a store that grants the permission, so Allowed=false can only come from the denial entry.

issues.description: A cached permission set that denies a resource always triggers a full DB permission reload, so checks over many inaccessible dashboards issue one query per resource instead of being served from cache.

earlierComments.text: Every distinct resource denied by the cached permission map triggers a reload of the entire user's action permission set, because the denial cache is resource-specific and a cached false result always falls through to getIdentityPermissions. Sequential checks of N inaccessible dashboards therefore execute N full permission queries and cache rewrites even with a current action-wide cache; getUserPermissions' singleflight only merges overlapping requests. Bound refreshes per user/action with a short refresh cooldown or generation marker so different resource misses can share a recent refresh.

issues.description: The Service struct comment listing its caches was not updated for the new permDenialCache field.

earlierComments.text: The struct doc comment still reads "// Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles", but this PR added the new `permDenialCache` field (line 58). The comment no longer enumerates what the struct actually holds and misleads a reader about the new denial-cache field; update it to mention the permission-denial cache so the prose matches the fields.

issues.description: Reminder cancel helpers are called without await inside forEach when bookings are cancelled/rescheduled or workflows edited, so the handler can return before reminders are cancelled or deleted and failures are unobserved.
issues.knownIssueText: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder called inside forEach without collecting/awaiting promises. WHY: handler returns before cancels complete and rejections are unobserved, so cancellations are lost and reminder emails/SMS are still sent (same fire-and-forget pattern repeated in handleNewBooking:966, bookings.tsx:488, workflows.tsx:212/376/519/574).

Cancellation now delegates the database update/deletion to asynchronous reminder helpers without awaiting them, while removing reminder deletes from the awaited promise list. The handler can finish before cancelled flags or unscheduled-reminder deletions are persisted, allowing a subsequent scheduler run to schedule a cancelled booking's reminder and leaving cancellation work unfinished when a serverless invocation terminates. Collect and await the helper promises; apply the same correction to the modified rescheduling and workflow-update callers that discard these promises.

Await the reminder cancellation promises before completing the cancellation request. These helpers now own persistence of cancellation: email awaits a workflowReminder update and SMS awaits Twilio before deleting the row. The forEach discards their promises, and removing remindersToDelete from the awaited promise list removes the previous guarantee that reminder state is cleared before the handler returns. In a serverless request the outstanding operations can be interrupted after the response, leaving reminders active for a cancelled booking. Collect these helper promises and include them in the awaited Promise.all.

issues.description: The cron cancels SendGrid sends for cancelled reminders in one try around the whole loop, so one failing cancel aborts all remaining cancellations and the row deletions, and the failing row blocks later runs.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: remindersToCancel loop awaits SendGrid cancel per-reminder inside one try and only runs Prisma deletes after the loop, with no method filter. WHY: a single throw (e.g. null SMS referenceId sent as batch_id, or one SendGrid error) aborts the loop and skips Promise.all deletes, leaving all other cancelled emails still scheduled so they are still sent.

Successful cancellation records are only deleted after every SendGrid request in the loop succeeds. If a later request fails, the catch skips all queued Prisma deletions; the next run retries an already-cancelled batch, which SendGrid rejects with 400, and aborts before processing the remaining reminders. Await each reminder's database deletion immediately after its successful cancellation and isolate errors per reminder so one failed batch does not block the others.

Handle cancellation failures per reminder rather than around the entire batch. If one SendGrid request rejects (for example, for an expired or invalid batch ID), the loop exits before cancelling the remaining reminders, and Promise.all is never reached, so even earlier successfully cancelled reminders remain in the database. The failed record stays eligible for the next run and can repeatedly block other cancellations until their emails are sent. Execute each successful deletion and isolate failures so the worker continues processing the remaining reminders.

issues.description: Email reminders for cancelled bookings are only flagged cancelled and cancelled in SendGrid by the cron later, so reminders close to their send time can still be delivered.

earlierComments.text: Deferred cancellation includes reminders less than ten minutes from their scheduled send time, when SendGrid no longer permits cancellation. A booking cancelled in that interval is only marked cancelled locally by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, and the cron's POST is rejected, so its email is still delivered. Process cancellation before SendGrid's ten-minute cutoff and explicitly handle cancellations that arrive after that deadline rather than relying on this cron query to stop delivery.

issues.description: The cron cancels SendGrid scheduled sends one at a time with sequential awaits, which is slower than batching.

earlierComments.text: The new cancel loop performs a sequentially awaited SendGrid HTTP request (`await client.request(...)`) for each reminder returned by an unbounded `findMany` (no `take`), then deletes them. WHY: this is O(N) serial network round-trips per cron run; if many reminders are cancelled at once (e.g. a bulk event-type disable or booking cancellation wave) the cron handler can block for a long time on serial SendGrid latency. HOW: fan the independent SendGrid cancel requests out with `Promise.all`, and/or bound the query with `take` plus pagination, then batch the DB deletes.

WHAT: SendGrid cancel issued with sequential await inside for loop over remindersToCancel. WHY: cron blocks O(N) sequential network round-trips instead of parallel batch, materially slowing the hourly schedule job as cancelled backlog grows.

issues.description: deleteScheduledEmailReminder and its immediateDelete flag do not delete anything; the names no longer describe the behaviour.

earlierComments.text: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and its `immediateDelete` flag no longer match what the code does. The default path only marks the reminder `cancelled: true`, and the `immediateDelete` path only sends a cancel request to the email provider. Neither path deletes the scheduled send or the row, unlike the SMS counterpart, which still deletes. Rename them (for example `cancelScheduledEmailReminder` and `immediateCancel`) or document the behaviour.

issues.description: deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the DB row only after a successful Twilio cancel, so a cancel failure leaves the reminder row behind now that callers no longer delete it.

earlierComments.text: twilio.cancelSMS and prisma.workflowReminder.delete share one try block. If the Twilio cancel throws, the DB row is never deleted. The reminder row then stays behind for a booking that was cancelled, rescheduled or deleted, because the callers no longer delete rows themselves. Delete the row in a finally block, or handle the cancel failure separately so the delete still runs.

issues.description: Prisma is imported in workflows.tsx but no longer used.

earlierComments.text: `Prisma` is imported as a value (line 9) but is no longer used anywhere in this file. This PR removed the only usages (`Prisma.BatchPayload` in the now-deleted `remindersToDelete` / `deleteReminderPromise` declarations), while the import was kept. WHY: the repo's ESLint `no-unused-vars` rule will fail CI/build for an unused import. HOW: remove `Prisma` from the import list (and keep `import type { PrismaPromise }` as a type-only import).

issues.description: The cron route sets the API key only on @sendgrid/mail, so the new @sendgrid/client cancellation requests are unauthenticated and reminders for cancelled bookings stay scheduled.
Leftover debug logs in the annotation cleanup emit Error-level entries with the full ID list on every batch, flooding error logs during normal operation.
issues.knownIssueText: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls r.log.Error on every cleanup batch (also duplicated at lines 554-557 and 576-579) dumping full ids slice, cond, and nil err at Error level. WHY: Fires Error-level log per batch and serializes up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs (32767 in new test), spamming error logs/monitoring on every normal cleanup run. HOW: Downgrade to Debug or remove; do not log full ids at Error.

WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` (and the identical Error-level logs for 'by count' and 'Tags to clean', lines 554/557/576/579) run on every batch in production. WHY: These log the full ID slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 elements) at Error severity on every cleanup iteration, flooding logs with false error noise and large payloads for a normal successful operation, and can trigger error-based alerting. HOW: Remove these log lines, or downgrade to Debug and drop the full `ids` slice (log only the count).

Avoid using Error-level logging on the normal cleanup path. The new r.log.Error calls emit count, ids, cond, and err at lines 534/537, 554/557, and 576/579 during non-error execution, creating log noise; consider downgrading or removing these logs on the normal path.

issues.description: The comment states SQLite's parameter limit is 999, which is only true for SQLite versions before 3.32.0.

earlierComments.text: The comment states that SQLite has a parameter limit of 999, but SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults to 32766 (as the added integration test also recognizes). This branch is choosing a conservative compatibility threshold, not expressing the limit of every SQLite database. Document 999 as the older-version/compatibility threshold so maintainers do not mistake this constant for the actual limit on modern SQLite.

issues.description: On MySQL and Postgres, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID without limit, so a cleanup batch size above 65535 makes every DELETE fail.

earlierComments.text: The bind-parameter workaround only handles SQLite's limit; the placeholder branch is used for every other engine with len(ids) placeholders and no bound. The previous implementation had no bind parameters, so this path is new. Postgres (extended protocol) and MySQL both cap bind parameters at 65535, so a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize larger than that makes this DELETE fail at Exec with a parameter-limit error instead of cleaning anything. Clamp the number of ids per DELETE (e.g. chunk into <=1000/<=65535 id sub-batches) for all dialects, not just SQLite.

On Postgres and MySQL, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID with no cap. A configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above the driver's bind-parameter limit (65535) makes every cleanup batch fail, and the cleanup job then never finishes. Split the IDs into chunks below the limit, or inline the integer IDs as the SQLite branch does.

issues.description: The SQLite inline ID list is built with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is quadratic in batch size.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: SQLite large-batch IN-list built with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. WHY: Quadratic string copying on large batches (e.g. 32767 IDs in added test) during cleanup, a background job path. HOW: Build with strings.Builder or strings.Join.

The SQLite literal-ID path rebuilds the entire accumulated string for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32,767 setting in the integration test, generate substantial repeated copying and allocation before each delete, consuming cleanup time and memory. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once.

issues.description: The cleanup service ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running every cleanup job ten times as often and increasing database load.
issues.knownIssueText: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no justification. WHY: Runs all 8 cleanup jobs including the new multi-query (SELECT+DELETE per batch) annotation cleanup 10x more often, multiplying DB load. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or justify the frequency change separately.

WHAT: The cleanup job ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. WHY: This runs all cleanup jobs (annotations, expired snapshots/versions/images, short URLs, query history) 10× more frequently, multiplying background DB load and lock contention — the opposite of the deadlock mitigation this PR targets — and appears to be a debug leftover unrelated to the described change. HOW: Restore the ticker to `time.Minute * 10`.

The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job runs. This job also drives the annotation/tag cleanup path changed in this PR, which now fetches ID batches into memory and emits Error-level logs per batch, so running it every minute substantially increases DB load and log volume with no functional benefit. Unless a 1-minute cadence is explicitly intended, this should stay at 10 minutes (it reads like a leftover from testing).

issues.description: The 'running the max count delete again' test case no longer runs cleanup a second time after the PR's per-subtest seeding and cleanup, so it does not verify that a repeated max-count cleanup deletes nothing.
The annotation cleanup loop stops on a batch whose IDs were already deleted by a concurrent cleaner, leaving the remaining work to the next cycle; checking the fetched count instead would avoid that.
MaxCount annotation cleanup reads victim IDs with LIMIT/OFFSET and deletes them in a separate non-atomic statement, so concurrent deletions can make it delete annotations that should be retained.
Delete puts the base d.Log instead of the enriched per-call logger into the context, so downstream logs lose name/kind/method fields.
issues.knownIssueText: The context is being created with d.Log instead of the log variable that was initialized with additional context values (name, kind, method). This means those values won't be propagated to the logging context.

earlierComments.text: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` installs the mode-level logger instead of the request-scoped `log` built on line 96 (which carries name, kind and method) — a copy/paste error, as every other method in this file passes the composed `log`. Storage.Delete and the legacy delete goroutine therefore log without the per-request fields this PR is adding (and without the metrics method/kind context).
ctx is built with klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) instead of the enriched `log`. The delete logs then lose the name, kind and method values. Use `log`.
The Delete context uses d.Log rather than the per-call log. This is a logging-context inconsistency (not a data leak); use the per-call logger for consistency.

issues.description: The legacy DeleteCollection goroutine records its duration with recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration, misattributing legacy latency and errors to the storage metric.
issues.knownIssueText: In DualWriterMode3's DeleteCollection method, when a storage operation fails, recordStorageDuration is incorrectly called with recordLegacyDuration instead.

earlierComments.text: The legacy DeleteCollection duration and error status are recorded in the unified-storage histogram. Every successful unified deletion therefore produces a second storage observation for a different backend, while legacy deletion failures are attributed to unified storage and no legacy observation is emitted. Call recordLegacyDuration here instead.

The timed call is d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, but its measurement is emitted using recordStorageDuration. Use recordLegacyDuration; otherwise storage receives two measurements for a successful collection deletion and legacy receives none, and legacy failures appear as storage failures.
The legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded with recordStorageDuration, so legacy latency and errors are attributed to storage. Use recordLegacyDuration.

issues.description: Delete's success path records the storage metric with the object name in the kind label instead of options.Kind, creating per-object series and inconsistent labels.
issues.knownIssueText: Inconsistency: using name instead of options.Kind for metrics recording differs from other methods.

earlierComments.text: The Delete success-path metric passes `name` where every other call site in this file (lines 48, 103, 113, 156, 159) passes options.Kind in the kind/name argument slot. The storage-success sample for Delete is thus labelled with the object name instead of the resource kind, breaking label consistency with the other operations and with the error sample emitted at line 103. Use options.Kind here (or insert name consistently everywhere, matching the metric's label semantics).
recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) at line 106 passes the object name in the kind label slot.

recordStorageDuration is called with the object `name` as the `kind` label: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`. Every other storage call site passes `options.Kind` (lines 73, 89, 103, 156, 159). This injects a per-object value into the kind label, corrupting the metric and giving it unbounded cardinality (one series per object name), which grows memory on every delete. Should be `options.Kind`.

issues.description: On storage Create/Update failure the duration is recorded with recordLegacyDuration, attributing unified-store errors to the legacy metric.

earlierComments.text: On a Storage.Create failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage) — the failing subsystem is Storage, not Legacy, and it passes the storage start time. This records storage failures under the legacy metric, corrupting the dual-writer error dashboards (and contradicts the success path on line 48 which uses recordStorageDuration). Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

On a Storage.Update failure the code records the error with recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage), attributing a storage failure and its storage duration to the legacy metric. This is inconsistent with the success path on line 132 (recordStorageDuration) and with mode1's semantics. Use d.recordStorageDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage).

The async goroutine performing the LEGACY DeleteCollection measures it with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy). Every other legacy write in this file uses recordLegacyDuration (lines 56, 113, 140); recording it under the storage metric reports legacy latency/errors as storage latency/errors. Use d.recordLegacyDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy).

issues.description: Mode 3 legacy writes now run in background goroutines derived from the request context, which is cancelled when the request completes, so legacy writes can be cancelled and legacy storage falls out of sync.

earlierComments.text: The async legacy write goroutine derives its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)). The apiserver cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns — which is immediately after Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection return — so the goroutine's Legacy.Create can be canceled before completing, silently dropping the legacy write that this mode exists to guarantee. The same applies to the goroutines at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167. Detach the async context from request cancellation (e.g. derive from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) / context.Background()) before applying the timeout.

The legacy write in Mode 3 became fire-and-forget, changing the contract callers relied on: previously Create (and, identically, Update/Delete/DeleteCollection) returned only after the LegacyStorage call had been made in-request; now it returns immediately and the write runs in a detached goroutine. Worse, the goroutine builds its context from the request-scoped `ctx` (line 51: `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`), which the API server cancels as soon as the handler returns/flushes the response — so the legacy write and its 10s timeout will typically be cancelled outright and the legacy store silently stops being updated, which is precisely what the new mode-3 integration cases assume still happens. Any detached work must be given a context not tied to the request lifetime (e.g. context.WithoutCancel(ctx) or a server-lifetime context), and consumers that depended on the synchronous legacy write need to be updated.

The asynchronous legacy write derives its timeout context from the request context, which is canceled when the HTTP request finishes. Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection return before this work completes, so their legacy database operations can be canceled immediately instead of receiving the intended ten-second window. Derive the bounded background context from context.WithoutCancel(ctx) to retain request values without inheriting request cancellation.

issues.description: Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo instead of a wrapper carrying the object stored in unified storage, so legacy recomputes the update and can diverge.

earlierComments.text: Legacy.Update receives the original objInfo instead of the object successfully committed to unified storage. The playlist legacy implementation calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, old) against its own legacy object, so a patch is reapplied to potentially stale state and can persist a different result or fail rather than mirror the unified write. Pass an updateWrapper containing res, as the previous implementation did.

Legacy.Update previously received an updateWrapper containing the object returned by Storage.Update; it now receives the original objInfo. UpdatedObjectInfo can compute an update from the old object supplied by each backend (notably for patches), so evaluating it against a stale legacy object can produce a different result or reject an update that already succeeded in Storage. Preserve the canonical-result contract by passing an updateWrapper with updated: res and upstream: objInfo to the legacy consumer rather than replaying the original update against legacy state.

Legacy.Update now receives the original objInfo rather than the updateWrapper containing the object successfully committed to Storage. UpdatedObjectInfo can represent a patch/transform based on the supplied old object; replaying it against legacy's potentially different old state can persist a different result or fail, even though the authoritative update succeeded. Restore forwarding of the committed result via updateWrapper instead of recomputing the update against legacy state.

issues.description: The Mode 3 tests never wait for or assert the asynchronous legacy writes, and legacy and storage share one mock, so removing the legacy calls would not fail them.

earlierComments.text: The legacy half of Mode 3 is never verified, so these tests cannot catch its removal. Mode 3 is documented as writing to BOTH LegacyStorage and Storage, and the implementation performs the legacy write in a detached goroutine (`go func(){ d.Legacy.Create(...) }()`, dualwriter_mode3.go lines 50-57, and likewise at 108-114, 134-141, 161-167). Each test registers legacy expectations (`setupLegacyFn`, e.g. lines 30-32 and 40-42) but never calls `m.AssertExpectations(t)`, `AssertCalled` or `AssertNumberOfCalls`, and never waits for or observes the goroutine — no channel, no polling. Additionally `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (lines 53-54, and the same pair in every other test function) share one `*mock.Mock`, so even a count assertion could not distinguish a legacy call from a storage call. Deleting every `d.Legacy.*` call from the implementation leaves all six tests passing, which is exactly the regression the names — and the Mode 3 contract — claim to cover.

The successful Create test never verifies the legacy write. Configuring m.On("Create", ...) does not require that expectation to be consumed, and these assertions only inspect the object returned by Storage.Create. Deleting the entire legacy-create goroutine would still pass this test. Use distinct storage and legacy mocks and synchronize on the legacy call, then assert that it completed with the intended object.

The successful Update case configures a legacy Update expectation but returns after checking only the unified-store result. It neither waits for the asynchronous legacy update nor verifies its expectation, so removing the legacy-update goroutine entirely still passes. Add explicit synchronization and verification of the legacy update (ideally with separate mocks), including the object propagated to legacy storage.

issues.description: The List error test case is still named 'not implemented' although List is now implemented and the case checks storage error propagation.

earlierComments.text: The test-case name "error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented" still describes the old stub List (which returned nil, nil with a "List not implemented" log). List is now implemented at dualwriter_mode3.go:79 and delegates to Storage.List; the case merely checks that a Storage error is propagated. The name contradicts the code it now exercises — rename it, e.g. "error when listing objects in the unified store fails".

issues.description: The Create test case name says 'only in the unified store' although Mode 3 also writes to legacy.

earlierComments.text: The test name says creation happens "only in the unified store", but this case configures a successful Legacy.Create as well, and Mode3.Create launches that legacy write after the unified write succeeds. Rename the case to describe creation in both stores (with the legacy write asynchronous), so test output does not communicate the opposite of the mode-3 write contract.

issues.description: Independent per-request goroutines remove ordering between legacy writes to the same resource, so legacy can end up with an older version or a resurrected object.

earlierComments.text: Independent goroutines remove ordering between successful writes to the same resource. For example, Storage commits update A and then update B, but the legacy goroutine for B can finish before A, leaving legacy with A while Storage contains B. Likewise a delete can run before an earlier create and leave a resurrected legacy object. Preserve per-resource commit order for mirroring (including across create/update/delete), rather than launching each write independently.

issues.description: The storage-failure Create test registers its failing expectation via setupLegacyFn and only works because legacy and storage share one mock.

earlierComments.text: The 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' case registers the failing Create expectation only through setupLegacyFn. It passes only because legacy and storage share one mock, so the storage Create gets that error by accident. Register the expectation in setupStorageFn and use separate mocks for legacy and storage, so the test really covers a storage failure.

issues.description: DualWriterMode3.Delete now returns on any unified-storage error, including NotFound, before deleting from legacy, so objects that exist only in legacy can no longer be deleted.
Mode 3 legacy-storage write errors (create/update/delete/delete-collection) are no longer logged after moving to async goroutines; only a duration metric with an error flag is recorded.

The postMessage handler in embed.js checks the sender with discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin), a substring test instead of exact origin equality, so a page on an origin that is a substring of the Discourse URL can send forged discourse-resize messages to the embedding page.
issues.knownIssueText: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.

earlierComments.text: The message-origin check uses substring matching: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`. Any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted (e.g. discourseUrl `https://discourse.example.com` accepts origin `https://discourse`), so a malicious page can post `discourse-resize` messages into the embed. Compare against the iframe's actual origin exactly (`e.origin !== expectedOrigin`) instead of a substring test.
Uses indexOf containment instead of origin equality, but it cannot be bypassed.

WHAT: postMessage origin check is reversed (`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1`) instead of strict origin equality. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, letting a foreign iframe drive `iframe.height` handling and future message branches.

issues.description: The referer and embed_url host checks compare against SiteSetting.embeddable_host case-sensitively, so a host differing only in case is rejected even though hostnames are case-insensitive.

earlierComments.text: Host identity is compared case-sensitively: `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer such as `http://EVILTROUT.COM/...` never matches the configured `eviltrout.com` (and the same flaw exists in lib/topic_retriever.rb:15 for `URI(@embed_url).host`). Normalize both sides with downcase before comparing so case variations of the same host are treated identically.

The referer/host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. The reviewer notes this fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the host comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections. The same issue applies to topic_retriever.rb.

The host comparison does not lowercase either side, so a mixed-case host is wrongly rejected. This fails closed and is not a bypass. Normalize case on both sides of the comparison (e.g. downcase both) to avoid false rejections.

issues.description: PollFeed reads i.content.scrub for every feed item, so items without a content element (common in RSS feeds that only have description) raise NoMethodError and abort the import of the remaining items.
issues.knownIssueText: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every feed item has a `content` element. WHY: many RSS 2.0 items expose only `<description>` (simple-rss returns nil for `content`), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and, because the job is `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the entire hourly feed import for all items is aborted. HOW: fall back to the available field, e.g. `(i.content || i.description || i.summary).to_s.scrub`, and skip items whose body is blank.

The feed item is consumed unconditionally: url = i.link, then i.title, and content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub). SimpleRSS item accessors raise NoMethodError when the element is absent (RSS 2.0 feeds frequently carry only <description>, no <content>, and some items have no <link>/<title>), so a single malformed or content-less item aborts the whole hourly job with an unhandled exception instead of skipping it. The code already anticipates a blank link (line 33 fallback) but reads i.content/i.title without a nil guard; use i.content.to_s (or fall back to i.description/summary) and skip items whose content is blank.

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError when a feed item has no content (only a description). The exception aborts the whole poll, so every item after it is never imported. Fall back to `i.content || i.description`, skip items with blank content, and rescue per item.

issues.description: Posts imported from RSS or remote pages use cook_method raw_html, which makes Post#cook return the raw HTML without sanitization, and the embed view outputs it with raw post.cooked, allowing stored XSS from imported content.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: the new `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` makes `Post#cook` return completely unsanitized HTML, and Jobs::PollFeed stores untrusted feed content this way (poll_feed.rb:35-36 → TopicEmbed.import, unlike import_remote which sanitizes via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist). WHY: the stored `cooked` value is then emitted with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and that page is served from the forum's own origin — so a malicious/compromised RSS feed item containing `<script>` or `onerror=` runs attacker JavaScript in the forum origin and can read cookies/session and perform authenticated actions (stored XSS). HOW: sanitize the raw HTML before persisting it (e.g. run the feed content through the same HTML sanitizer used for regular posts, or restrict the raw_html cook path to trusted, pre-sanitized sources only).

WHAT: Post#cook returns raw verbatim for cook_method raw_html, skipping the cooking/sanitization pipeline and plugin filters. WHY: any RSS/readability HTML imported via TopicEmbed is rendered unsanitized in embed/best.html.erb, executing attacker script in the Discourse origin.

Feed-provided HTML is persisted with raw_html cooking after only Nokogiri parsing and URL rewriting, which do not sanitize scripts or event-handler attributes. A malicious feed entry containing executable HTML is stored as post.cooked and executed under the forum origin when rendered, including through the new raw cooked embed view. Sanitize imported HTML with an explicit safe tag, attribute and URL-scheme allowlist before storing it or returning it from the raw_html cooking path.

issues.description: TopicEmbed.import appends a footer that interpolates the URL unescaped into an <a href='...'> tag in raw HTML that is later rendered unsanitized, so a crafted URL can inject markup; it also appends to contents with << without handling nil.
issues.knownIssueText: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into raw HTML (`#{url}`) and stores feed HTML as raw_html. WHY: url passing /^https?\:\/\// can still contain `'`, `>` or script, and RSS content is never sanitized, giving stored XSS when rendered via `raw post.cooked`. HOW: HTML-escape url and sanitize content instead of raw_html passthrough.

TopicEmbed.import interpolates feed-controlled url unescaped into HTML link stored with cook_method raw_html (Post#cook returns raw, bypassing pipeline) and rendered with raw post.cooked: XSS via quote/script break-out. Escape url for text and attribute contexts before storing.

The url is interpolated unescaped into `#{url}`. The post is stored with cook_method raw_html and rendered with `raw post.cooked`, so a url containing a quote or markup is output as live HTML. Escape it with ERB::Util.html_escape (or CGI.escapeHTML) for both the href and the link text.

issues.description: TopicEmbed.import appends the footer with contents <<, mutating the caller's string in place instead of building a new string.

earlierComments.text: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place. This raises FrozenError for frozen strings and appends the footer twice if the same string is imported again. Use `contents = contents + ...` instead.

issues.description: TopicEmbed.import checks for an existing embed and then creates the post and TopicEmbed without handling the unique-index conflict, so two concurrent imports of the same URL make one job fail with RecordNotUnique.

earlierComments.text: TopicEmbed.import does a check-then-insert on embed_url (where(...).first, then TopicEmbed.create!) with no rescue for the unique index declared on topic_embeds.embed_url. The only guard against concurrent intake is the Redis throttle in TopicRetriever, which is bypassed for staff (retrieve_topic.rb:17 passes no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)) and can expire while a slow retrieval (which may synchronously run a full PollFeed, topic_retriever.rb:41) is still running. Two interleaved retrievals for the same URL both see embed.blank? and both attempt creation; the loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, which is unhandled anywhere in the job path, breaking execution. Guard the create against the race (rescue/retry on RecordNotUnique, or use find_or_create_by on embed_url inside the transaction) so concurrent retrievals cannot raise.

Make creation idempotent under concurrent imports. Two workers can both read no embed at line 15 and create posts before attempting the same unique embed_url insert. The unique index correctly rolls back the losing transaction, but its unhandled uniqueness exception aborts that job (and potentially the rest of a feed polling run). This is reachable when scheduled polling overlaps retrieval-triggered polling; the per-URL retrieval throttle does not serialize those paths. Handle the conflict outside the transaction and return the winning embed/post, or serialize imports for the URL.

Race on check-then-create: two concurrent imports both see TopicEmbed.where(embed_url:url).first blank, both create Post + TopicEmbed.create!. Unique index on embed_url then raises RecordNotUnique (unhandled) or creates duplicates. Need atomic find-or-create / rescue unique violation.

issues.description: When the embedded post has been deleted, TopicEmbed.import's update path passes a nil embed.post to PostRevisor and crashes on every later import of that URL.

earlierComments.text: On the update path `embed.post` can be nil if the post was deleted. `PostRevisor.new(nil)` then raises NoMethodError, and every later import of that URL fails the same way. Guard against a nil post, for example by skipping the revision or recreating the topic.

WHAT: update path uses `embed.post` without nil guard then `PostRevisor.new(post)`. WHY: if the first post was deleted, post is nil and revise! dereferences nil, crashing feed-poll updates instead of recreating/skipping.

Orphan-post crash on update path: post = embed.post can be nil if the post/topic was deleted, then PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError. Must handle missing post (recreate or skip) instead of assuming present.

issues.description: Claims import_remote crashes on unparseable pages (nil content) and dead URLs because it does no nil check or network error handling around open(url).read.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: import_remote passes `doc.content` (and title) directly to import where `contents <<` assumes a String, with no nil check or network-error handling around `open(url).read`. WHY: unparseable pages (nil content) raise NoMethodError and dead URLs raise OpenURI errors, crashing RetrieveTopic/Disqus imports with no topic created.

issues.description: absolutize_urls only handles root-relative paths: protocol-relative URLs like //cdn.example.com/x.png are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/x.png and path-relative links are left unresolved, breaking links and images in imported posts.

earlierComments.text: The URL rewrite treats protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/image.jpg` as paths on the article host, producing `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/image.jpg`. Imported images and links using protocol-relative external URLs therefore point to the wrong server. Resolve both href and src using URI joining against the article URL, which also handles ordinary relative paths correctly.

Resolve relative href/src references with URI joining rather than handling only leading slashes. For an article at http://example.com/blog/article, href='next' and src='images/photo.jpg' remain relative and resolve against the forum instead of the imported article. Moreover, '//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg' is rewritten to 'http://example.com/cdn.example.com/photo.jpg'. Both yield incorrect links/images in imported posts; apply proper URI resolution to both anchors and images.

absolutize_urls treats any href or src starting with '/' as site-relative and strips all leading slashes. Protocol-relative URLs like '//cdn.example.com/a.png' are rewritten to 'http://site/cdn.example.com/a.png', which is broken. Skip values starting with '//' (or prefix them with the scheme) and only rewrite single-slash paths.

issues.description: The embed view formats post dates with a hard-coded strftime pattern, so users in non-English locales see English month names and a fixed order while the rest of the view is translated.

earlierComments.text: The post date uses a hard-coded strftime format `"%e %b %Y"`. `%b` emits English month abbreviations (Jan, Feb, ...) no matter what locale the viewer is in, so the date is frozen to en-US while the surrounding strings in this same view are localized via I18n.t. This is a locale-pinned user-facing format; it should be localized (e.g. via the app's localized date helper / l( ) rather than a literal strftime pattern).

Use a localized date formatter rather than strftime("%e %b %Y"). %b produces English month abbreviations and the fixed day-month-year order ignores the selected locale, although the neighbouring header and footer labels are translated. Embedded comments therefore show English-formatted dates for users of other locales.
Date uses strftime("%e %b %Y") hard-coding one locale's month names/order while neighbouring strings go through I18n.t. Use I18n.l with a locale date format so non-English users see localized dates.

issues.description: The Disqus importer now creates topics through TopicEmbed.import_remote, dropping the thread's created_at and the category option and requiring a live HTTP fetch per thread, so imported topics get wrong dates/categories and a dead link aborts the import.

earlierComments.text: WHAT: Disqus import replaced PostCreator (title/raw/created_at/category) with `TopicEmbed.import_remote` per thread, dropping category_id, created_at, and strip handling. WHY: imported topics lose categories/timestamps and now require a live HTTP fetch per thread, failing when links are dead.

Preserve the Disqus thread creation timestamp when switching to TopicEmbed.import_remote. The previous PostCreator call passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])`, but this replacement passes only the title, and TopicEmbed.import_remote/import never forward a timestamp to PostCreator. Imported historical topics now get the migration time as their initial post creation date while their replies retain historical dates, losing the importer's chronological fidelity. Extend the import options to forward created_at and pass the thread timestamp here.

The Disqus import now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote instead of PostCreator. This silently drops the `--category` option and the `created_at` from the Disqus thread, and the `--category` method_option was removed from the CLI. It also now makes a live HTTP fetch of every thread link, and `open(url)` raises on a failure that previously could not happen, aborting the whole import. Keep the category and date handling, and rescue fetch errors per thread.

issues.description: Every retrieval of an article not yet embedded synchronously polls and imports the entire RSS feed, and since throttling is per URL, many different article requests repeat the full feed download and processing.

earlierComments.text: Every uncached article retrieval synchronously downloads and processes the complete configured feed before fetching the article. Because the retrieval throttle is keyed by individual embed URL, simultaneous requests for different articles each repeat the feed download and all per-item database lookups/imports, multiplying worker load by the number of requests times feed size. Coalesce feed polling with a feed-wide throttle or lock and reuse its recent results instead of executing a full poll per article.

issues.description: The 'is 404 without an embed_url' spec never sets an embeddable host, so the request is rejected by ensure_embeddable before the embed_url check runs, and the test would pass even without that check.

earlierComments.text: The test is named 'is 404 without an embed_url' but passes for the wrong reason: it never sets embeddable_host, which defaults to '' so the before_filter `ensure_embeddable` raises at the blank-host check before `params.require(:embed_url)` is reached. The request is rejected regardless of whether the embed_url requirement exists, so the test would still pass if that requirement were removed. Stub a valid embeddable_host here so the failure is actually attributable to the missing embed_url.

The missing-embed_url test does not establish a valid embeddable host and referer, so ensure_embeddable rejects this request before best reaches params.require(:embed_url). It also only checks non-success despite claiming a 404. Removing the required-parameter check would therefore leave this test green. Configure an allowed host/referer for this case and assert the intended missing-parameter response.

The 'is 404 without an embed_url' test never sets embeddable_host, so ensure_embeddable rejects the request before params.require(:embed_url) runs. It passes without the embed_url check. Stub embeddable_host and the referer so the missing param is the only failure cause.

issues.description: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' specs leave feed_polling_enabled at its false default, so they never reach the condition they name and would pass with those checks deleted.

earlierComments.text: The three 'requires ...' tests do not isolate the guard they name: each stubs only one setting to falsy while the other two remain falsy by default, so poll_feed is never called even if the named check were deleted. Stub the other two settings to truthy values in each test so removing the named guard would cause poll_feed to run and fail the test.

These two tests do not verify the conditions they name. `execute` is guarded by `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`, and feed_polling_enabled defaults to false. Neither test stubs feed_polling_enabled? to true, so the guard short-circuits at the first clause and poll_feed is never called no matter what feed_polling_url/embed_by_username are. Both would still pass if the URL/username checks were deleted entirely. Stub `SiteSetting.stubs(:feed_polling_enabled?).returns(true)` in each so the specific condition under test is actually reached.

The URL and username prerequisite tests never enable feed polling (whose configured default is false) or supply the other required setting. execute consequently short-circuits at feed_polling_enabled? and never evaluates the prerequisite each test claims to cover. Both tests still pass if their corresponding presence checks are removed. Set all other prerequisites to valid values before making only the setting under test absent, so the poll_feed.never expectation actually detects removal of that guard.

issues.description: PollFeed.feed_key computes a per-feed cache key that is never used, so the feed is re-fetched and re-processed every hour without a modified-since check.
The embed layout references the 'embed' stylesheet and embed.js, but neither is in config.assets.precompile, so with precompiled assets in production the embed page fails to load them.
The retrieve throttle is keyed by the full embed URL, so an anonymous client can vary the query string on the embeddable host to bypass it and make the server create an unbounded number of topics.

The "requires feed_polling_enabled?" spec leaves feed_polling_url and embed_by_username at their blank defaults, so poll_feed is skipped regardless and the test would pass even without the enabled check.
TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches the embed URL with open(url).read and no timeout or size limit, so a slow or huge remote page can block the background job and exhaust memory.
The retrieve throttle sets the Redis key with setnx and sets its TTL in a separate expire call, so a crash between the two leaves a key without expiry that blocks retrieval of that URL forever.
`import_remote` fetches the embed URL with open-uri, which follows redirects, so the embeddable-host check on the initial URL can be bypassed to reach internal services (SSRF).

PostMover#copy recreates the first post via PostCreator without passing cook_method, so a moved raw_html (embedded/imported) first post is re-cooked through the markdown pipeline and its content changes.

earlierComments.text: `PostCreator` now supports a `:cook_method` option, but `PostMover#copy` (app/models/post_mover.rb:57-62) copies the first post with `PostCreator.create(raw: post.raw, ...)` and does not pass `cook_method: post.cook_method`. Moving the first post of an imported topic, which has cook_method raw_html, therefore re-cooks its HTML through markdown, so the copy's cooked content can differ from the original. Pass `cook_method: post.cook_method` in `PostMover#copy`.

issues.description: EmbedController#best renders the 'loading' placeholder and still calls discourse_expires_in 1.minute, so the anonymous cache stores the placeholder under the embed URL and visitors keep seeing 'Loading Discussion...' for up to a minute after the topic exists.

earlierComments.text: The 'loading' placeholder is rendered and then `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` still runs, so the anonymous cache stores the placeholder under the real embed URL. Anonymous visitors can keep seeing 'Loading Discussion...' for up to a minute after the topic has been created, and the 30s auto-reload can hit the same cached page. Call discourse_expires_in only in the branch where @topic_view was built, not when rendering 'loading'.

issues.description: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create in Topic.transaction, so PostCreator's post-transaction job enqueueing (process_post, feature_topic_users, etc.) runs before the outer transaction commits, and a worker that picks up ProcessPost early finds no post and skips post-processing for the imported topic.

earlierComments.text: Wrapping `PostCreator#create` in `Topic.transaction do` defeats the job-enqueue ordering that `PostCreator` explicitly relies on. `PostCreator#enqueue_jobs` (lib/post_creator.rb:288) is deliberately called after its own transaction with the comment "We need to enqueue jobs after the transaction. Otherwise they might begin before the data has been comitted", but the nested `Post.transaction` joins this new outer transaction (no savepoint), so `trigger_post_process`/`feature_topic_users`/`after_post_create` are enqueued while the post/topic/embed rows are still uncommitted. A Sidekiq worker that picks up `Jobs::ProcessPost` before commit finds no post and silently returns (app/jobs/regular/process_post.rb:11), losing onebox/image post-processing and notifications for the imported topic. Enqueue the jobs after the `Topic.transaction` block commits (e.g. create the topic/post/embed inside the transaction but call the post-create jobs outside it).

issues.description: The migration adds posts.cook_method with a default and NOT NULL in one add_column, which on the PostgreSQL versions of the time rewrites the whole posts table under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock and blocks reads and writes during deploy.

earlierComments.text: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` rewrites the entire `posts` table while holding an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the PostgreSQL versions in use at the time (the ADD COLUMN-with-default fast path only landed in PG 11). On any non-trivial forum this blocks all reads and writes to `posts` for the duration of the migration during deploy. Add the column as nullable first (or with a default applied in a separate backfill), then set the default/`NOT NULL` afterwards.

issues.description: OptimizedCursorPaginator passes negative cursor offsets straight into Django queryset slicing, which Django does not support, so requests with a negative offset raise an error instead of returning a page.
issues.knownIssueText: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

earlierComments.text: The advanced negative-offset branch passes a negative slice start directly to a Django QuerySet, which does not support negative indexing. A cursor such as 0:-1:0 is accepted by Cursor.from_string but crashes the optimized audit-log request instead of providing reverse pagination. Reject negative offsets with BadPaginationError or implement reverse traversal using nonnegative slices and reversed ordering.

The comment claiming that Django ORM 'properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false: Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative indices. This branch passes cursor.offset straight into queryset[start_offset:stop], so it raises rather than supplying the documented negative-offset pagination. Correct the negative-offset support claims here, in the class docstring, and in the new BasePaginator boundary-handling comment (or implement actual supported boundary handling) so callers are not promised a pagination mode that the underlying queryset cannot provide.

Django QuerySets do not support negative slice bounds. Passing a negative cursor offset directly into `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises an exception instead of enabling advanced pagination. Validate or normalize negative offsets before slicing, or implement reverse traversal through ordering/filtering rather than negative slices.

issues.description: The comment added to BasePaginator claims negative offsets are allowed and safely handled by the queryset, but the code clamps non-prev offsets to zero and leaves prev offsets as before, so the comment misdescribes the behaviour.

earlierComments.text: The added comment says this change will "allow negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination ... safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions", but the statement it annotates, line 182, is `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` — it clamps negative offsets to 0, i.e. it does the opposite of what the comment claims and leaves the 'negative offset' (offset < 0) paging behaviour exactly as before. The comment is now untrue for the code it sits on; either drop the 'allow negative offsets' wording or make the code actually permit them.

The comment declares this change `allow[s] negative offsets to enable efficient bidirectional pagination`, but the actual computation is `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, which clamps non-prev offsets at 0 — i.e. it never permits a negative offset. The declared optimization is a no-op relative to the original `queryset[offset:stop]`; the comment describes behavior the code does not have.

BasePaginator now passes the raw `offset` to the slice whenever `cursor.is_prev` is true (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). A negative offset from a user-supplied prev cursor therefore reaches `queryset[negative:stop]`, which Django rejects. This crashes every endpoint that uses BasePaginator. Fix: always use `max(0, offset)`, or validate the offset when the cursor is parsed.

issues.description: The OptimizedCursorPaginator docstring claims streamlined boundary handling, an optimized query path and backward compatibility that the implementation, a copy of BasePaginator plus a negative-offset branch, does not provide.

earlierComments.text: Docstring lists 'Streamlined boundary condition handling', 'Optimized query path for large datasets', and 'maintaining backward compatibility', but get_result (845-886) is a copy of BasePaginator with only a negative-offset branch added — no streamlined handling or optimized path exists, and negative-offset slicing breaks prior cursor semantics. Doc describes behavior the function does not produce — align doc to code or implement the claimed handling.

issues.description: OptimizedCursorPaginator computes cursor keys with math.floor/ceil on the raw attribute, but the audit log endpoint uses it with order_by='-datetime', so building the cursor raises TypeError for any non-empty result.
issues.knownIssueText: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

earlierComments.text: OptimizedCursorPaginator requires numeric integer keys (get_item_key uses math.floor/ceil + int, cursor_value defaults to 0) but is instantiated here with order_by="-datetime". This mismatched producer/consumer contract breaks pagination for datetime-ordered audit logs. Fix: do not use OptimizedCursorPaginator for datetime ordering; keep DateTimePaginator or make OptimizedCursorPaginator datetime-aware.

WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key/value_from_cursor mishandles datetime ordering by calling math.floor/ceil directly on a datetime and returning raw int cursor value. WHY: Used with order_by="-datetime" it crashes with TypeError on floor(datetime) when building cursors and filters the datetime column against an int in build_queryset, breaking pagination. HOW: Copy DateTimePaginator logic — timestamp via strftime/multiplier with floor/ceil and convert cursor value back with datetime.fromtimestamp.

The optimized branch selects a numeric-key paginator while ordering by the datetime field. On any nonempty first page, build_cursor invokes OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key, which calls math.ceil on a datetime and raises TypeError; nonzero cursors also lack the datetime conversion provided by DateTimePaginator. Make the optimized paginator inherit DateTimePaginator or preserve its timestamp encoding and decoding.

issues.description: The audit log endpoint always dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access, which crashes with AttributeError for authorized token requests that have no member, even on the default pagination path.
issues.knownIssueText: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.

earlierComments.text: The unconditional advanced-access check dereferences organization_context.member although RpcUserOrganizationContext permits member=None.
